purpose: Buyer education layer for the practical reality of owning a used motorcycle today. Values are model-specific where source-backed and otherwise explicitly marked as a benchmark or coverage-gap.

global_defaults.planning_efficiency_method: Use owner-reported or ARAI/claimed efficiency when sourced. Where only claimed efficiency exists, MotoWorth may use 85% of claimed as a transparent planning estimate; it is not a prediction of actual mileage.
global_defaults.parts_availability_policy: Never claim local stock from brand reputation alone. Show a support signal and tell the buyer to verify current local availability, especially for discontinued models or specialist parts.

service.note: Hero's service manual states paid service is due within 180 days or 6,000 km, whichever comes first.

parts.note: Hero describes a wide service network and easily available spare parts for the Splendor family.

hero-splendor-plus.ride_today: Low running-cost profile; particularly practical when the bike is being used frequently for city commuting.
why_now: Fuel efficiency is unusually strong for a petrol motorcycle, which matters more as annual kilometres rise.
The maintenance cadence and parts ecosystem are straightforward for an everyday commuter.
pause: Do not overpay merely because it is a familiar brand; condition, age and service history still determine the individual bike.
If the bike has neglected chain, brake, tyre or oil maintenance, the headline fuel economy will not rescue a poor ownership example.

sources.label: Hero MotoCorp — Splendor Plus mileage & ownership

service.interval_note: Service schedule varies by generation; check the exact owner's manual and stamped/job-card history for the year being purchased.

parts.note: Royal Enfield provides a service-centre and genuine-parts locator; local stock can still vary by city and part.

re-classic-350.ride_today: A practical middleweight when you value easy access to support and a relaxed riding experience more than outright performance.
why_now: A current, widely supported model family can reduce the friction of routine service and consumables.
Owner-reported fuel economy around the mid-30s km/L can keep running costs reasonable for a 350cc motorcycle.
pause: A used Classic can span very different generations; do not use today's model reputation to price an older generation automatically.
Verify the exact service schedule, clutch/chain/brake condition and any upcoming tyre replacement before closing.

service.network_note: Honda offers maintenance contracts for its BigWing motorcycle network; local service capacity should be checked by city.

parts.note: Honda provides an AMC/service framework for BigWing motorcycles; verify local parts stock for model-specific items.

honda-cb350.ride_today: Balanced ownership profile: moderate fuel consumption with a relatively manageable 350cc running footprint.
why_now: The model can make sense for regular use when service history is clear and the local BigWing support channel works for you.
Owner-reported mileage around 35 km/L keeps fuel spend from becoming the main ownership problem for moderate annual usage.
pause: Do not treat the Honda badge as proof that a particular used bike was maintained well.
Ask for the exact service record and confirm parts/service availability in your city before buying a bike with unresolved issues.

service.note: Verify the exact service schedule for the bike's year and the current availability of specialist support before purchase.

parts.note: The GSX-S750 is discontinued in India. Parts availability and lead times should be verified for the exact year/part before paying a scarcity premium.

suzuki-gsx-s750.ride_today: An enthusiast-focused litre-class-adjacent experience with materially higher fuel spend than commuter or 300–400cc bikes. Its discontinued status makes parts/support verification part of the purchase decision.
why_now: A well-maintained example can still make sense when the buyer specifically wants its four-cylinder character and the local support picture is acceptable.
The used-bike decision should focus heavily on condition, records and parts verification rather than comparing it with a brand-new motorcycle on headline price alone.
pause: Do not pay extra simply because a seller calls it 'rare'. The model is discontinued, so scarcity is not the same thing as verified market premium.
Before closing, verify availability and lead time for expensive or model-specific parts, and inspect the cooling, electronics, brakes, suspension and drivetrain carefully.
At roughly 19 km/L in reference testing, fuel can become a meaningful recurring cost for high-mileage daily use.

efficiency.note: Mileage is intentionally not hard-coded until a current model/year-specific source is verified.

service.package_note: Kawasaki currently publishes a ₹46,500 K-Care price for Ninja 650; its published 8-service EW+Service figure is ₹55,588.

parts.note: Kawasaki's service programme uses genuine parts; local part lead times should still be checked for specific items.

kawasaki-ninja-650.ride_today: More important to budget for service and consumables than to chase a single mileage figure. Kawasaki's current published K-Care price makes scheduled servicing a visible, estimable cost component.
why_now: A current model with a published service package makes scheduled maintenance easier to budget than an unsupported or fully discontinued motorcycle.
For buyers who want a middleweight twin and can absorb premium-bike consumable costs, ownership can be planned rather than guessed.
pause: Confirm K-Care eligibility/scope for the specific used bike; a current package price is not automatically transferable to every used example.
Check tyre, chain/sprocket and brake condition because these consumables can materially change the first-year ownership bill.

service.note: Triumph publishes 16,000 km / 12 months, whichever comes first, for the Scrambler 400 X.

parts.note: Use the authorised network for model-specific service; verify local stock for specialist parts before buying a damaged example.

triumph-scrambler-400x.ride_today: A performance-oriented single that can work as a daily-plus-weekend bike when the buyer accepts a mid-20s-to-high-20s km/L fuel profile.
why_now: The published 16,000 km/12 month service interval can make scheduled servicing easier to plan.
Its fuel-efficiency references are in the high-20s km/L range, which is manageable for moderate mileage.
pause: Do not use owner-reported mileage as a guarantee; traffic, throttle use and maintenance can move actual consumption materially.
Check the exact service history and local availability of model-specific parts before buying a bike with unresolved electrical, suspension or crash damage.

efficiency.note: Mileage is not hard-coded until a current India-market source is verified.

parts.note: Ducati's authorised network and genuine-parts servicing are an important part of ownership; consumables such as tyres, brake pads and clutch components are outside the quoted Ducati Protect packages.

ducati-monster.ride_today: This is a premium performance ownership decision. The right question is not only resale value but whether the buyer is comfortable with premium-service and consumable economics.
why_now: Ducati currently publishes explicit service-package pricing, which makes a portion of scheduled maintenance costs visible upfront.
Longer oil and valve-clearance intervals can reduce how frequently the motorcycle needs major scheduled attention, although consumables remain separate.
pause: Do not mistake long service intervals for low total ownership cost; tyres, brake components and other consumables can be significant.
Verify whether any Ducati service package or warranty benefit transfers to the specific used motorcycle.

parts.note: Verify local parts stock, lead times and specialist support before purchase.

fallback.ride_today: MotoWorth is still expanding model-level ownership data. Treat the price output as incomplete until the ownership profile is source-backed.
why_now: A clean, documented example can still be interesting when the ownership basics are confirmed locally.
pause: Do not pay a premium for assumed reliability, rarity or brand image until the model/year evidence is verified.
